compiled_state.description:
## Context

Discovered while widening the MCP model/schema drift gate for mirror F5
(`62eb-5e6f-512a-420d`). That gate's registry covered 11 of 32 public `*Out` models. Deriving
the registry — every model whose `<snake_case>.schema.json` exists — brings 9 more models under
the check, and four of them are ALREADY DRIFTED.

## The measured gap: 41 undeclared schema properties

- **CreateResultOut** (create_result.schema.json) — 1: `title`
- **GateResultOut** (gate_result.schema.json) — 5: `ac_items`, `criteria_count`, `file_impact`, `keyword_count`, `line_count`
- **NextBatchOut** (next_batch.schema.json) — 12: `available_pool`, `batch`, `batch_size`, `epic_title`, `skipped_blocked`, `skipped_blocked_story`, `skipped_design_awaiting`, `skipped_in_progress`, `skipped_manual_awaiting`, `skipped_needs_planning`, `skipped_overlap`, `tasks`
- **TicketStateOut** (ticket_state.schema.json) — 23: `attestations`, `author`, `bridge_alerts`, `bridge_project`, `close_class`, `close_reason`, `completion_expectation`, `created_at`, `creation_channel`, `creation_channel_inferred`, `detected_by`, `env_id`, `force_close_reason`, `last_reopened_at`, `preconditions_summary`, `repos`, `reverts`, `source_author`, `source_created_at`, `source_env`, `source_id`, `updated_at`, `verify_commands`

## Why this is separate from F5

F5 fixes the GATE — it makes the check enum-aware and derives its registry so nothing can be
silently omitted again. Closing these 41 gaps is a different change with a different risk
profile: `_mcp_models` supplies the MCP tools' published `outputSchema`, so declaring a field
CHANGES THE WIRE CONTRACT clients read. That deserves its own review rather than riding along
inside a gate refactor.

F5 therefore baselines these four models as declared exceptions naming THIS ticket, so the gate
is green at rest while any NEW omission fails. Standard ratchet shape, the same one
`check_complexity_baseline.py` and `check_mechanism_delta.py` use.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: each of the four models declares the properties its canonical schema defines, or the
      schema is corrected where the property is genuinely not part of that payload. Verified by
      the drift gate reporting zero missing declarations for them with their baseline entries
      REMOVED.
- [ ] AC2: the baseline exception entries added by F5 are deleted, not merely emptied, so the
      gate's exception map returns to naming only genuine permissive omissions. Verified by
      grepping the gate for this ticket id and finding none.
- [ ] AC3: any property deliberately NOT declared carries a stated reason in the gate's
      permissive-omissions map. Verified by reading each remaining entry.
- [ ] AC4 [non-codebase]: the wire-contract impact is stated — for each newly declared field,
      whether MCP clients could already observe it in practice. Verified by a comment on this
      ticket recording the assessment.

## Testing

- `python -m rebar.schemas.check_mcp_models --check` — zero drift with the baseline removed.
- `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_model_schema_drift_heldout.py -q`.
